n1bd20f02c3c.s: Which of the following is NOT correct about religious patronage in the Ikshvaku kingdom?
o: Wealthy lay women funded stupas and viharas
Kings were the chief patrons of stupas and viharas
Queens and princesses supported Buddhist monuments
n1bd20f02c3c.x: The Ikshvakus showed dual patronage: kings performed Vedic sacrifices, while royal and wealthy lay women funded Buddhist stupas and viharas.

n9c39492c42b.s: Which of the following pairs relating to Nagarjunakonda is correctly matched?
n9c39492c42b.x: The site was discovered in 1926 by A. Ranganatha Saraswati; Longhurst worked in 1927–31, Ramachandran in 1938 and the rescue excavation ran 1954–60.

new.s: Who was the first woman donor recorded at Nagarjunakonda?
new.x: Chamtisri, sister of Sri Santamula, was the first woman donor; Bodhisri was ranked first among women donors.

new.s: How many ayaka pillars did Chamtisri donate at the Maha Chaitya of Nagarjunakonda?
new.x: Chamtisri gave 9 ayaka pillars along with 170 dinari-masakas.

new.s: Chamtisri's gift recorded at Nagarjunakonda included how many dinari-masakas?
new.x: Chamtisri donated 170 dinari-masakas besides 9 ayaka pillars.

new.s: Princess Kodabalisri built a vihara for monks of which Buddhist sect?
new.x: Kodabalisri, daughter of Virapurushadatta, built a vihara for the Mahishasaka monks; Bhatti Mahadevi's vihara was for the Bahushrutiya.

new.s: Which of the following donor–gift pairs is INCORRECTLY matched?
o: Bhatti Mahadevi – Vihara and chaitya for the Bahushrutiya
Harmyasri – Vihara for the Mahishasaka monks
new.x: Harmyasri gave a pillar for her mother; the Mahishasaka vihara was built by Kodabalisri.

new.s: Queen Rudradhara Bhattarika, who donated an ayaka pillar, was the daughter of:
new.x: Rudradhara Bhattarika was the daughter of Rudrasena of Ujjain; Bodhisri was the daughter of Revanta of Amaravati.

new.s: Bapisri and Chatisri, who gave pillars at the Mahachaitya, were related to Virapurushadatta as his:
new.x: Bapisri and Chatisri were queens of Virapurushadatta and daughters of his aunt.

new.s: In the donative inscriptions, Adavi Chamtisri is described as the ____ of Virapurushadatta.
new.x: Adavi Chamtisri was the sister of Virapurushadatta and gave an ayaka pillar at the Maha Chaitya.

new.s: In which language are most ayaka-pillar donative inscriptions at Nagarjunakonda written?
new.x: Most donative records at Nagarjunakonda are Prakrit ayaka-pillar inscriptions of Virapurushadatta's 6th regnal year.

new.s: Which dynasty was the first to date its records by year, month and day?
new.x: The Ikshvakus were the first to date their records by year, month and day.

new.s: The inscription of Upasika Bodhisri at Nagarjunakonda is evidence of:
new.x: Bodhisri was a non-royal donor, so her record shows non-royal patronage of Buddhism.

new.s:
Consider the following statements about the gifts of Vasishthiputra Sri Santamula:
1. He gave gold, cows and ploughs.
2. He gave agraharas to Brahmins brought from the north.
3. Part of his revenue went to overseas colonies.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
new.x: He gave gold, cows, ploughs and land and agraharas to northern Brahmins; revenue went to tanks and canals, not overseas colonies.

new.s: Where was the Ashvamedha altar of Vasishthiputra Sri Santamula found?
new.x: The Ashvamedha altar of Santamula is at Nagarjunakonda.

new.s: In Ikshvaku inscriptions, the Poosika Sreni was a guild of:
new.x: Poosika Sreni were sweetmeat traders; Parnika Sreni were betel-leaf traders.

new.s: In Ikshvaku records, the term Telika referred to:
new.x: Sale, Telika and Kammaru meant weavers, oil pressers and blacksmiths respectively.

new.s: Which of the following was imported into the Ikshvaku region?
new.x: Gold, silver, wine and glassware were imports; spices, iron, coconuts and cotton textiles were exports.

new.s: The Roman-style amphitheatre of the Ikshvaku period is located at:
new.x: A Roman-style amphitheatre stands at Vijayapuri, evidence of Roman contact.

new.s: Brahmadeya grants under the Ikshvakus were exempt from how many taxes?
new.x: Brahmadeya grants were exempt from 18 taxes, helping Brahmins become a landlord class.

new.s: The practice of cross-cousin marriage in Andhra began with the:
new.x: Cross-cousin marriage began with the Ikshvakus.

new.s: Ikshvaku princess Kodabalisri married a ruler of which dynasty?
new.x: Kodabalisri married Vishnurudra Sivalananda Satakarni of the Chutus.

new.s: Which of the following is NOT correct about Ikshvaku society?
o: Records show matronymics such as Vasishthiputra
Records mention the practice of sati
Brahmins lost land under the Brahmadeya system
new.x: Brahmins rose through Brahmadeya grants and became a landlord class; the other statements are recorded.

new.s: Which was the only Ikshvaku king to adopt Buddhism?
new.x: Virapurushadatta alone adopted Buddhism; the other kings performed Vedic sacrifices.

new.s: Upasika Bodhisri served Buddhism during the reign of:
new.x: Bodhisri served Buddhism in the reign of Ehuvala Chamtamula (APPSC G2 2012 key).

new.s: Vasishthiputra Sri Santamula worshipped Virupakshapati and:
new.x: Santamula worshipped Virupakshapati (Shiva) and Mahasena (Skanda); Hariti was the tutelary deity.

new.s: A sculpture showing a Shivalinga trampled underfoot is linked with which Ikshvaku king?
new.x: Virapurushadatta, the Buddhist king, is linked with the sculpture of a Shivalinga trampled underfoot.

new.s: Which of the following is NOT correct about Ikshvaku religion?
o: Puranic Shaivism, Vaishnavism and Shakti worship thrived
Virapurushadatta performed Vedic sacrifices as a Buddhist
Royal women funded stupas and viharas
Shantisri and Harmyasri were sisters of Santamula
new.x: All kings except Virapurushadatta performed Vedic sacrifices; he adopted Buddhism.

new.s: Hariti, the tutelary deity of the Ikshvakus, was worshipped as the protector of:
new.x: Hariti was the protector of children, and bangles were offered to her.

new.s: Which of the following Buddhist sect–centre pairs is correctly matched?
new.x: Purvasailiya was centred at Amaravati and Aparasailiya at Nagarjunakonda.

new.s: Acharya Bhadanta Ananda, who knew the Digha and Majjhima Nikayas by heart, belonged to which sect?
new.x: Acharya Bhadanta Ananda belonged to the Aparamahavinaseliya sect.

new.s: The vihara of Bhatti Mahadevi at Nagarjunakonda was built for which sect?
new.x: Bhatti Mahadevi, mother of Ehuvala, built a vihara for the Bahushrutiya.

new.s: The phrase 'Samma Sambudhasa dhatuvara parigahita' at the Maha Chaitya shows that it enshrined:
new.x: The Maha Chaitya is a Dhatugarbha stupa over the Buddha's bodily relics.

new.s: How many ayaka pillars did Chamtisri add when she rebuilt the Maha Chaitya?
new.x: Chamtisri rebuilt the Maha Chaitya in Virapurushadatta's 6th year with 9 ayaka pillars.

new.s: Which of the following was NOT among the countries named in Bodhisri's inscription as receiving the Dhamma?
new.x: Her inscription names Kashmir, Gandhara, China, Chilata, Tosali, Aparanta, Vanga, Vanavasi, Yavana, Damila and Palura; Magadha is not listed.

new.s: According to the Mahavamsa, who took Buddhism from the Pallava-bhoga region to Sri Lanka?
new.x: The Mahavamsa credits Mahadeva Bhikshu with taking Buddhism from Pallava-bhoga to Sri Lanka.

new.s: Which Ikshvaku king set up the Sriparvata University?
new.x: Virapurushadatta set up the Sriparvata University.

new.s: Acharya Nagarjuna was a philosopher of which school?
new.x: Nagarjuna was the Madhyamika philosopher after whom Sriparvata (Nagarjunakonda) is named.

new.s: Who built the Sarvadevadhivasam temple at Nagarjunakonda?
new.x: Commander Elisiri of Ehuvala built the Sarvadevadhivasam, with a Sanskrit inscription.

new.s: The Sarvadevadhivasam temple at Nagarjunakonda was dedicated to:
new.x: Elisiri's Sarvadevadhivasam was built for Kumara Swami (Kartikeya).

new.s: Which is regarded as the first Vaishnava temple in Andhra?
new.x: The Ashtabhuja Narayanaswami temple, built by the Abhira commander Shivasena, is the first Vaishnava temple in Andhra.

new.s: The Pushpabhadraswami Shiva temple was started by Virapurushadatta and completed by:
new.x: Pushpabhadraswami was started by Virapurushadatta and finished by Ehuvala.

new.s: In May 2025, Miss World contestants visited which Buddhist site next to Nagarjunakonda?
new.x: Miss World contestants visited Buddhavanam, part of the Integrated Buddhist Circuit, in May 2025.

new.s: In April 2026, the Palnadu Collector proposed a boat service between Nagarjunasagar and:
new.x: On 2 April 2026 the Collector visited the Nagarjunakonda Museum and proposed a Nagarjunasagar–Srisailam boat service.

new.s: The first depiction of sati in Indian art is found in the sculpture of:
new.x: The Sati panel of the Ikshvaku period at Nagarjunakonda is the first depiction of sati in Indian art.

new.s: Nagarjunakonda represents which phase of the Amaravati School?
new.x: Nagarjunakonda is the final, most mature phase of the Amaravati School, with Mahayana themes.

new.s: The favourite themes of Nagarjunakonda sculpture were the Buddha's life and:
new.x: Nagarjunakonda sculpture shows Mahayana themes – the Buddha's life and Jataka stories.

new.s: A Paribhogika stupa is built over:
new.x: Paribhogika stupas enshrine objects used by monks such as alms bowls; Dhatugarbha enshrine relics; Uddeshika enshrine nothing.

new.s: How many pillars stand on each ayaka platform of the major stupas at Nagarjunakonda?
new.x: Ayaka platforms in the four directions carry five pillars each.

new.s: Which of the following is NOT a part of the Agamic temple plan followed by the Ikshvakus?
new.x: The Agamic plan has garbhagudi, antarala, mantapa, dhvajastambha and prakara; ayaka platforms belong to stupas.

new.s: The town of Yeleswaram is credited to which Ikshvaku commander?
new.x: Commander Elisri, who also built the Sarvadevalaya, is credited with Yeleswaram.

new.s: At Vijayapuri, the Rajaprasadam refers to:
new.x: Rajaprasadam and its prakaras formed the palace complex; Kummakundam were tanks.

new.s: The Swarna Devalayam inscription, the first Sanskrit record of Andhra, belongs to which regnal year of Ehuvala Santamula?
new.x: The Swarna Devalayam record is of Ehuvala's 11th regnal year.

new.s: Ehuvala Santamula's Gummadidurru record in Guntur is written in:
new.x: Although Ehuvala introduced Sanskrit, his Gummadidurru record is in Prakrit.

new.s: From which century CE did Sanskrit replace Prakrit in Ikshvaku inscriptions?
new.x: Sanskrit replaced Prakrit from the 4th century CE after Ehuvala Santamula brought it in.

new.s: Who wrote the Kuvalayamala?
new.x: The 8th-century Kuvalayamala is by Udyotana.

new.s:
Consider the following statements about Buddhist literature linked to Nagarjunakonda:
1. Acharya Nagarjuna wrote Madhyamika works.
2. The Kuvalayamala records foreign students at Dhanyakataka and Nagarjunakonda.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
new.x: Nagarjuna wrote the Suhrllekha and Madhyamika works; Udyotana's Kuvalayamala records foreign students at both centres.

new.s: Which archaeologist is associated with the 1938 work at Nagarjunakonda?
new.x: T. N. Ramachandran worked at Nagarjunakonda in 1938; Longhurst worked in 1927–31.

new.s: Who was among the excavators of the 1954–60 rescue excavation at Nagarjunakonda?
new.x: R. Subrahmanyam was among the excavators of the 1954–60 rescue excavation.

new.s: After which year was the Nagarjunakonda valley submerged by the Nagarjuna Sagar reservoir?
new.x: The valley was submerged after 1960.

new.s: The ASI rebuilt the transplanted monuments of Nagarjunakonda at Anupu, on the bank of which river?
new.x: Monuments were rebuilt at Anupu on the Krishna bank and on Nagarjunakonda island.
